newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea's top cabinet job seen changing hands.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's top cabinet job seen changing hands.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam is expected to name a new prime minister on Tuesday, an informed government source said on Monday.
The source declined to give details on Kim's choice to replace current premier Lee Soo-sung, but newspapers on Monday tipped a university president with extensive cabinet experience.
Leading dailies unanimously picked Koh Kun, 59, president of Seoul's Myongji University, as the most likely candidate.
Kim has launched a sweeping reshuffle of his administration aimed at restoring his reputation badly tarnished by a scandal involving loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co.
Last Friday, he replaced his chief secretary and three other top aides at the presidential Blue House.

An extensive reshuffle of cabinet positions, including the key finance ministry job, is widely expected after Kim names a new prime minister. The National Assembly must approve the selection of premier.
Current prime minister Lee was plucked from the presidency of Seoul National University by Kim in 1995.
Kim apologised last Tuesday over a loans-for-kickbacks scandal at Hanbo, which went bankrupt on January 23 after piling up debts of $5.8 billion.

Koh served as mayor of Seoul from 1988-1990 during the presidency of Roh Tae-woo. He was minister of Home Affairs, Transportation, Agriculture and Forestry under the previous administration of Chun Doo Hwan during the early 1980s.
He took up his university post in 1994.
